executions or all-lines approval.

**Verified defects.** The API's subject-confined discovery continuation encodes
AuthorityId, canonical SubjectKey and MembershipId with reversible base64url.
Copying it into entry JSON, links and hidden fields disclosed the server-only
association material when the entry had more than twenty qualifying Memberships.
This granted no bearer or scope, but violated the existing confidentiality rule.
Separately, impossible/noncanonical base64url reached self lookup and became a
configuration 503 rather than input 400.

**Correction.** Native entry uses the established Node crypto AES-256-GCM library
with one independent random 32-byte cursor-only key, fresh 12-byte IV, full
16-byte tag and fixed version/purpose plus actual owner/host/epoch authenticated
data. This implements ADR-0078's server-only custody; it creates no configured
credential, permission or context authority. The API contract remains private
and unchanged. A maximum 739-byte ASCII plaintext plus envelope fits the existing
1,024-character browser bound; the actual API's 184-character cursor produces a
284-character continuation. No per-page map, eviction or queue is introduced.
The [Node 22 crypto contract](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v22.x/api/crypto.html)
owns primitive behavior; independent counterexamples exercise tag/AAD failures.

Unwrapping occurs after current entry/proof validation and before API work or
selection phase changes. The API still independently binds its cursor to the
verified subject and rechecks admission. Malformed/foreign/old continuations
refuse as input. Publication/logout/expiry/close clear and zero the owned key
buffer while retaining unsettled work credits. This is owned-buffer cleanup,
not a heap-wide erasure claim. Browser-safe canonical grammar checks length and
unused trailing bits without introducing Node imports into the public graph.
Upstream response validation remains strict.

choices and private mutation/account-change recovery share this pool. Current

product cleanup. The 27-copy source-map census is inventory, not execution of
every compiled branch. The exact private sources, chronology and original
failed-run evidence remain retained.

**Selected proposal.** Keep compression and native actual-operation ownership.
Patch all 27 pipe copies, common bundled compression and both CJS/ESM routers;
accurately regenerate associated source maps. Reserve an immutable response
owner slot synchronously at compression middleware entry. Observe actual
selection/terminal/stream closure and forbid duplicate or late creation. The
pipe and router both join its original promise; direct end cannot bypass it.
Do not release real end work, native handlers, issued writes, registered framework
work, API or snapshot owners from a transport close or timeout. Preserve primary
request failures while retaining separate cleanup faults; otherwise successful
work with failed cleanup fails. No source-loader monkeypatch, postinstall store
mutation, compression disablement or silent version fallback is selected.

**Three-step delivery and review order.** Each step is committed, independently
reviewed in R1, corrected/committed, reviewed by new R2 agents, then corrected and
validated before progression. Acceptance is not runtime qualification.

1. Accept ADR-0083 only with maintainer approval; move its Proposed index row to
   Active. Apply the exact carrier texts below, keep the new rule Registered,
   and update only Phase 03's Status for packet state. Preserve every Accepted
   body/status/date; add the own-record navigation amendment.
2. Add the deterministic parsed patch generator, qualified original/patched
   census, accurate maps, exact-version pnpm manifest/lock identity and frozen
   installation controls. Extend supported build, native dev/production,
   copied-proof and packaged entry points with fail-closed checks before Next
   import/listen. Produce/apply in an isolated staging tree; never mutate the
   shared store. Prove duplicate/missing/late slot, real construction/stream
   error, primary-plus-cleanup error, no-compression/HEAD/empty body, gzip/deflate,
   native backpressure and early-close paths. Exercise every changed semantic
   copy or an equivalent parsed semantic comparison plus the actual supported
   development/production route families. The generated minified diff size is
   a disclosed maintenance cost, not an excuse to omit a copy or stale map.
3. Prove unchanged native handler/write/framework/API/snapshot lifetimes with
   real held owners, actual router/static/streamed early-close and healthy
   requests, actual stock browser trilogy/counter witness, development native
   controls, frontend type/lint/full guard and public browser/Lighthouse proof.
   Register Implemented status only after decisive controls pass. Resolve the
   separate NoPlan corrections and freeze actual source/tree, toolchain, plan
   and newly discovered population. Complete and retain all 27-job/20-natural-
   owner/25-original-ZIP A, independently audit it, then full B on the identical
   freeze. Both layouts require exact zero-skip selected/executed/TRX unions.
   Original failed runs, partial siblings and failed-only reruns qualify none.

### ADR-0083 proposal R1 corrections and revised package (2026-11-01)

Two fresh independent proposal reviewers examine `d3b6981c`. Maintenance review
approves its scope and independently verifies all 27 runtime/map pairs, marker
census completeness and retained private source hashes. Ownership review finds
three Major decision ambiguities and one Minor proof omission. These findings
are verified and corrected in the Proposed ADR; no package/runtime policy is
implemented. Both original reports remain retained.

**Error-order contract.** A router rejection before encoding selection seals
its slot and permanently disables later compression creation before joining.
With no actual stream, that compression obligation needs no future response
terminal. Its captured uncompressed writer remains subject to the existing
native fence, allowing the caller's existing pre-header error response without
a circular wait. Real abort with a live response requests actual response
cancellation first. A normal return cannot seal away stream creation still
owned by registered response-producing work. This is a failed-operation path,
not permission for detached writes after ownership ends.

**Construction and stream faults.** Immediately observe owner rejection and
stream errors, including before the first join. Account for every actually
created resource; request actual stream/response cancellation and await real
stream close before settling failed cleanup. A compressor fault may terminate
the connection before any HTTP error body is sent. This is a disclosed transport
failure, not a changed ordinary API/BFF denial status. Duplicate/late creation
remains refused before allocation. Preserve a primary request error's identity
and separately retain cleanup failure; no unhandled rejection or lost owner
is licensed by the two finally joins.

**Irreversible wire.** A cleanup fault fails handler/cleanup ownership even if
headers or the complete HTTP response have already reached the peer. Already
sent status/body cannot be rolled back. No second response or synthetic rollback
is emitted. Retain the failed cleanup result and original publication fence;
never infer a clean handler from successful wire delivery or vice versa.

**Acceptance-carrier refinement.** The original three-step package and all
unchanged carriers remain. The following proposed texts replace the ambiguous
error/proof clauses for acceptance; the earlier Proposed record is history.

- Standard 07 adds: “Before-selection router rejection seals against later
  compression creation and retires only the empty compression obligation before
  propagating the error to the existing fenced native error boundary. Real
  abort/stream fault requests actual cancellation before join; construction
  errors account for every created stream. Observe faults immediately and join
  actual close. Preserve primary error identity and separately retain cleanup
  failure. Cleanup can fail after successful wire delivery; no already-sent
  status/body is retracted, second response emitted or rollback fabricated.”
- Testing 06 and Step 2/3 explicitly require: “Run a real initialized router with
  pre-header/pre-selection handler rejection and close/abort before selection,
  proving error propagation, no circular wait and no late stream allocation.
  Cover actual synchronous construction failure, fault before join and combined
  primary/cleanup failure, including absence of unhandled rejection. Exercise
  already-terminal attachment, close during a blocked write and during end,
  independent held write/end callbacks and drain, paired-listener retirement,
  and actual finish/close without fabricated events/callbacks. Faults before
  headers, after headers and after finish respect the irreversible wire boundary
  and preserve the original native output fences. Healthy wire/backpressure
  remains equal; no observation timeout acknowledges actual cleanup.”
- The existing new Registered catalogue rule includes those decisive error-order,
  event-order and independent-operation controls. Status promotion still waits
  for actual implementation/proofs; no separate rule or relaxed gate is added.

The prototype's nine controls remain mechanism evidence only. It does not
implement the synchronous reserved-slot and error-order refinements or initialize
the patched router. Full code, maps, package installation, actual native held
owners and complete fresh final-source hosted A/B remain required. Two new
independent proposal R2 reviewers inspect these corrections and the complete
proposal. Maintainer approval remains necessary before any dependency/runtime
implementation; manual accessibility evidence stays deferred and unexecuted.

  Mutating, deleting or adding boundary code refuses or triggers a genuine

### P03-4 document review and proposed decision package (2026-11-04)

**Proposed; approval pending.** The maintainer requests `/implement-task` on
`development`, existing-document review before implementation, up-front decisions
and a complete step plan. Every implementation step commits, receives two fresh
independent review rounds, fixes confirmed findings in new commits and then
continues automatically. New ADRs require explicit approval before their code.
This package starts no runtime, migration, provider change or CI workload.

Baseline is `e1339a39`, a clean `development` tree after the user-merged PR #40.
Existing P03-3 final-head B/original-archive and deferred manual evidence remain
as recorded in its merge closeout. They neither become completed nor authorize
waiving P03-4's proof. Settings and existing stashes remain untouched.

**Problem and phase fit.** P03-4/D06 completes the path from an administrator's
scoped offer to a verified new/existing person's Membership in that exact
institution/branch. It owns C08, its C01 invitation entry and C20 screen proof.
Keycloak authenticates/verifies accounts; Identity owns the offer and grant;
Tenancy owns lifecycle and the bounded lifetime setting; central Audit owns
required evidence. There is no invitation implementation to extend by merely
turning on a route.

amendments and governing Standards 01/04/05/07/08/11/13/16/18/19/21 sections.

The committed realm pins Keycloak 26.6.2, email mappers and SMTP to existing

Two independent initial read-only audits cover security/atomicity/data owners

| Confirmed gap or promise | Proposed action / owning carrier |

| G8 is Open; ordinary native entry needs existing Membership and global-self has exactly three descriptors | Separate exact invitation admission, host/offer witness and finite consumers; ADR-0093, Standards 05/11, source/caller census |

#### Proposed finite operation surface

These names describe implementation obligations, not existing endpoints. All API
paths carry `/api/v1`. No arbitrary native proxy, browser bearer or Server Action
is added. Input bodies are strict and at most 8 KiB; no unknown/duplicate fields
or supplied actor/tenant/org authority is accepted. Lists use 20 default/100
maximum, opaque actor/scope/operation-bound cursors and bounded no-store pages.
The exact serialized DTO/OpenAPI and byte/deadline checks land with each writer.

| API operation | Application consumer / capability and response |
|---|---|
| GET `/identity/invitations` and `/{id}` | `ListInvitationsQuery` / `GetInvitationQuery`; applicable membership-admin, exact current write scope, MUST read; email/Role/state/expiry/version, never verifier or raw link |
| GET `/identity/invitable-roles` | `ListInvitableRolesQuery`; same capability/scope, current-delegable ID/key/scope/version only, MUST read; no grant graph |
| POST `/identity/invitations` | `CreateInvitationCommand`; normalized email + one Role/version, exact current context, fresh delegation; protected keyed 201 version receipt/Location |
| POST `/identity/invitations/{id}/revocations` | `RevokeInvitationCommand`; fresh target authority, canonical If-Match, protected keyed bounded receipt |
| POST `/identity/invitations/{id}/handoffs` | `PrepareInvitationHandoffCommand`; current delegation, fixed Role pin, canonical If-Match; one secret response, rejects Idempotency-Key; explicit replacement renews generation/expiry |
| GET `/tenancy/settings/invitation-policy` | Tenancy-owned bounded 14-day/default-or-configured policy read through its contract; own-current-tenant coverage, Off; no arbitrary setting value |
| PUT `/tenancy/settings/invitation-policy` | `SetTenantInvitationLifetimeCommand`; Tenant setting-write and orgless, canonical If-Match/protected replay; one TenantSetting root, 1–30 days, MUST setting update |
| POST `/identity/invitation-entry/inspections` | `InspectInvitationQuery`; strict body ID/code, exact native/host/subject/offer admission; current verified recipient, Off physically ReadOnly; bounded own offer/Role/scope labels/version |
| POST `/identity/invitation-entry/acceptances` | `AcceptInvitationCommand`; strict ID/code/observed version, fresh provider proof and locked authority; natural offer/actor convergence, no generic Idempotency-Key; exact Membership/result/version receipt |
| POST `/identity/invitation-entry/results` | `GetOwnInvitationResultQuery`; strict ID/code, exact same Active actor/original Active Membership and consumed verifier; Off physically ReadOnly. No current-email/inviter/Role/expiry requirement for an already committed result, no new mutation intent. The acceptance dispatcher may select this exact read before mutation dispatch when its preflight already observes Accepted. |
| Internal original Invitation receipt read | `ReadInvitationReceiptQuery`; fresh exact admin target disclosure and MUST read; no token, mutation replay or successor substitution |
| Internal original lifetime-policy receipt read | `ReadInvitationPolicyReceiptQuery`; exact original TenantSetting ID and fixed key, orgless own-Membership coverage, MUST read; no generic setting directory or old write-permission requirement |

Native exact routes add localized `/studio/invitations`, invitation detail and
lifetime controls, plus the fixed localized invitation landing and clean
confirmation. Closed auth POSTs cover capture/inspect, verification, accept,
create/revoke/handoff and lifetime changes. They retain exact Origin/CSRF,
immutable response ownership and current session/scope. The new invitation
continuation can coexist with a live session, but cannot replace another subject.
Existing `canManageMemberships` applicability can expose the corresponding link;
no advisory Boolean becomes a grant. Exact private route/operation census lands
before activation; provider verification accepts only its fixed action/purpose,
not arbitrary OIDC parameters or destinations.

creation and five-minute continuation budgets are explicit accepted costs, not

### P03-4 Step 7 hosted browser-start and cleanup-masking correction (2026-11-06)

[Hosted run 42123447985, attempt 1](https://github.com/HodeTech/LearnStack/actions/runs/42123447985)
binds head `82573d60` and finishes with 24 successful jobs and three failures:
ordinary 2, ordinary 3 and the integration aggregate they refuse. Every
Architecture partition passes, so the census repairs hold. Ordinary 2 records
the browser/session fact at `browser-devtools-missing`; ordinary 3 records the
invitation-registration fact at `retained_tree`. No other case fails.

Both facts, and the entry-pagination fact, are the cases that start stock
Chromium, and they recur. Of the seven hosted runs on this PR whose retained
results were inspected, four contain one: `browser-devtools-missing` in runs
41977090425 and 42123447985 (it is also the 2026-10-26 record above),
`retained_tree` in 41957367950 and 42123447985, and an entry-pagination failure
with no retained reason in 42057464800 attempt 3. The public-admission browser
fact does not fail in the retained results. Failing and passing observations
occur on the same runner images and kernel, so neither correlates. Each fact was
met with a diagnostic and a clean local recheck; none with a change to the
failing path.

The retained evidence shows what can be said. In ordinary 2 the browser fact
runs alone from 22:55:12 to 22:55:48 and is the shard's first Chromium. Its
cleanup ends with the process terminated by a signal and no forced stop, so the
owned browser was live and responsive but published no port file in ten
seconds: a stall, not a crash. A probe with the same flags publishes the port in
about 0.4 seconds locally (Brave on macOS). Why it stalls on hosted runners is
not established.

`retained_tree` has a mechanism that is established. The invitation facts hold
the driver in `await using`, and C# replaces the exception in flight with the
one disposal throws. A control that fails after `ready` and leaves a private
directory makes the previous driver throw exactly the hosted message in place of
the fixture's own closed failure. The failure it hid in ordinary 3 cannot be
recovered from the retained artifacts. The Chromium step is the one thing the
registration fact has and the existing-identity fact (passing in all six
observations) lacks, but that is a correlation, not a proof.

The correction changes two things and no budget. `startBffBrowser` replaces a
browser that stayed live through the readiness window without a usable port file
(missing, empty or malformed) at most once: the stalled owned group is stopped
without force, then a fresh process starts on a fresh profile. Browser death,
owner closure, unreadable state and every failure after the DevTools port stay
single-shot, and a stall that cannot be stopped cleanly keeps its original closed
failure. The ten-second window, flags, sandbox, environment and cleanup limits
are unchanged. This is the infrastructure-flake retry that
[Testing Standards § Flaky Tests](../standards/06-testing.md#flaky-tests) allows
only with a logged justification: launching the test tool is not the behaviour
under proof, and the stall is independent of the product. Both native Chromium
fixtures use it. Separately, driver disposal keeps the first failure it raised
and only marks it when cleanup also fails; a cleanup-only failure still throws,
and `StartAsync`/`BrowserAsync` keep their strict form for their own observers.

Twelve new controls cover the stall predicate, the one-replacement bound, the
refusals above and an actual owned process group. The full web suite passes 3,753
cases; typecheck, lint and formatting pass. The disposal control passes and fails
without the driver change. The real invitation-registration fact passes locally in
36 seconds, and in 45 seconds when its first Chromium is forced to publish no port:
the first browser is stopped unforced, a second starts and the private tree is
removed. The browser/session fact itself was not run locally because port 3000
is held by the maintainer's running dev server, which is untouched.

The stall cause and hosted behaviour remain unproven. Same-source hosted A/B and
independent original-archive qualification remain open before delivery/merge.

[Hosted run 42238072858, attempt 1](https://github.com/HodeTech/LearnStack/actions/runs/42238072858)
binds head `93fd1f59` and finishes with 23 successful jobs, one failed ordinary
partition, one cancelled Architecture partition and the two aggregates that refuse
them. The analyzer correction holds: every shard builds, and meta, OpenAPI diff,
secret scan, frontend and public demo pass. One case fails in the whole run and no
shard reaches its test window. Two unrelated things are red.

Ordinary 0 fails the invitation-registration case with the closed reason
`browser-devtools_cleanup_failed` at `bff_native_driver` lines 213 and 287: the
fixture reports stage `browser-devtools` and then a failed session cleanup. This is
the Chromium start stall again, and the previous correction never took effect.
`stopTestChild` sends SIGTERM to the owned group and SIGKILL when the group is still
present after two seconds, and reports that stop as forced. The correction required an
unforced stop before replacing a stalled browser, so a stalled browser that did not
answer SIGTERM got no replacement, and the final disposal counted the same cached
forced stop as failed cleanup. Its unit control for the refusal encoded the same
assumption. With real owned processes, the previous code reproduces exactly that pair
for a start-up that ignores SIGTERM, and the corrected code starts the replacement and
disposes cleanly.

The stall cause is still not established. In the failing shard even
`google-chrome --version` took nine seconds where the other eleven shards took zero to
six. Of the three stalls that can be identified (the two earlier browser/session
records and this one), two ran in the shard with the slowest of those twelve
measurements and one, at one second, did not. A cold start may explain some stalls but
not all, so the correction does not rest on it.

The correction widens the retry and keeps the proof. `retireChild` on the fixture owner
releases one child once its whole group is confirmed absent, forced or not; `dispose`
is unchanged and still keeps the tree after a forced stop of any other child.
`startBffBrowser` retires a stalled browser through it and allows up to two
replacements, three launches in all, instead of one. Each DevTools wait is 20 seconds
instead of ten: the helper's maximum, and the window the public-admission fact already
uses without a stall in any inspected run. Nothing after the DevTools port is retried,
and a stalled group that cannot be confirmed absent keeps its closed failure. The
native driver's response budget for the entry and invitation browser phases is 150
seconds instead of 90, as it already was for the browser/session result; the
fixtures' 180- and 240-second deadlines and the driver's four-minute deadline are
unchanged. The passing browser/session fact takes 90.8 seconds on hosted, so the worst
accepted start (two full waits with their retirements, then a slow third start) ends
near 155 seconds. This is the infrastructure-flake retry that
[Testing Standards § Flaky Tests](../standards/06-testing.md#flaky-tests) allows with a
logged justification, on the same grounds as before: launching the test tool is not the
behaviour under proof. It supersedes the "without force", "at most once" and
"ten-second" statements of the
[previous record](#p03-4-step-7-hosted-browser-start-and-cleanup-masking-correction-2026-11-06),
which stays as what was believed then.

New controls cover a real owner retiring a start-up that ignores SIGTERM and then
disposing cleanly, the same owner still failing disposal for an unretired child that
needed SIGKILL, the three-launch bound and its closure, refusal when retirement cannot
be confirmed, and the owner's refusal of unowned children and of a closed owner. The
real invitation-registration fact passes locally in 45 seconds, and in 66 seconds when
its first browser is replaced by a start-up that ignores SIGTERM (the stand-in ran
twice, so the replacement ran). The browser/session fact was not run locally because
port 3000 is held by the maintainer's dev server.

Architecture 5 passes its cases and ends its execution step at 15:09:33. Its evidence
upload then starts and never ends: the step's own one-minute timeout does not fire,
GitHub cuts the job at the 45-minute ceiling and no log exists for any step. In the
four most recent runs every other upload step takes at most two seconds, and no
repository code runs in that step. This is recorded as a hosted-runner loss, not
repaired. The shard's evidence is missing, so the aggregates refuse and the run
cannot count toward qualification.

The stall cause and hosted behaviour of this retry remain unproven. Complete same-source
hosted A/B and original-archive qualification remain open.

## P03-5 — Custom fields and privacy classification

### P03-5 proposed custom-field contract and plan (2026-11-10)

**Proposed; no implementation or gate acceptance.** The maintainer selects
P03-5 through `implement-task`, development only, with a document/code decision
pass before implementation. Each meaningful step has an implementation commit,
two fresh independent review rounds and committed verified corrections. No
Astra reviewer is selected. A new architectural decision requires explicit
maintainer approval; routine implementation choices within it do not.

The inspected baseline is `d012e75a` on development with a clean working tree;
its P03-4 merge and closeout are local commits ahead of the last observed remote
tracking ref. No checkout, reset, merge, runtime/configuration mutation or CI
dispatch is part of this decision pass. Prior packet evidence and manual-check
limitations remain as recorded in their own closeouts.

#### Reverified existing contract and action list

- P03-5 depends on delivered P03-2/3, not the later provider/operator packets.
  G9 is Open. D07/D08 and C09/C10/C20 own definitions, values, classification,
  privacy and usable localized forms; P03-10 owns fulfillment, not this schema.
- Customization owns immutable target-qualified definitions; Identity owns
  values inside MembershipProfile. No such definition/value/consent model or
  writer exists at this baseline. The User model stays free of tenant data.
- ADR-0043 and the actual validator require nonempty object-root properties.
  A one-property `value` envelope reuses all four admission gates. The proposed
  finite nested form profile narrows admission without changing the evaluator.
- Existing Customization base/mapping cannot be reused unchanged: published
  labels can be renamed and indexes lack target. The new aggregate freezes all
  interpretive metadata and uses target-qualified historical/live constraints.
- Exact definitions already have uncached same-ambient, Active-at-read eligibility.
  Immutable historical pins permit that boundary without a new cross-module
  publication/commit guarantee.
- Existing Membership creation makes an empty Profile, including invitations and
  seed. Required custom fields are proposed as form-completion requirements,
  not retroactive membership, sign-in or invitation prerequisites.
- Data Protection assigns append-only purpose consent to Tenancy, but supplies
  no executable consent writer. A real, closed personal capture/withdrawal slice
  is proposed here. Existing OwnMembershipRead explicitly grants no write power.
- Current admin APIs/native/SDK strictly parse scalar profile fields, finite
  operations and nine advisory capabilities. New payloads need explicit typed
  extensions; no arbitrary JSON proxy or tenth capability follows implicitly.
- The general 256 KiB schema ceiling does not fit a 16 KiB native form. The
  proposed profile uses smaller logical input/actual encoded limits and bounded
  pages/values. Missing/null/default, nested shape and history behavior are
  explicit choices rather than assumed JSON Schema side effects.
- Existing grant registration is distinct from adoption. Proposed registry v3
  grants only the new Tenant definition-admin pair through explicit adoption;
  warm seed and startup never restore or expand grants.

These checks use the phase contract; Architecture 13/23/32; Customization,
Identity and Tenancy module specs/matrices; ADR-0043/0073–0079; applicable
Standards 04/05/07/08/11/16/18/19/21; and the current aggregate, schema validator,
authorization, audit, SDK and Studio/native implementations. Independent initial
reviews cover contract/privacy and experience/transport. They are static reviews,
not database, provider, browser or performance qualification.

#### Maintainer decision surface

[ADR-0095](../decisions/0095-revision-pinned-membership-custom-fields.md) proposes
one coupled decision:

- Membership-only, tenant-wide definitions; immutable successor revisions and
  exact value pins. Retired entries stay interpretable, read-only and removable;
  no key reuse, auto-migration or carryover to a revoked Membership's successor.
- A finite scalar/nested form profile, explicit required PII category with no
  default, no Payment or materialized defaults; requiredness does not block
  account/membership admission. The visual general builder remains Phase 06.
- Tenancy-owned personal sensitive-purpose consent with explicit withdrawal,
  sequence/predecessor fencing and separate truthful commits. Withdrawal hides
  retained values; it is not erasure or a recall of already disclosed bytes.
- One Tenant definition-admin pair with opt-in v3 grants. Existing profile-write
  holders gain custom-value writes within their existing exact target ceiling.
- Finite authoring/storage/transport limits, conservative whole-value diagnostic
  exclusion, current replay/disclosure authority and unchanged CI/runtime clocks.

No technical policy question is delegated to an implementation reviewer. If a
later verified finding needs a different accepted decision, its concrete change
returns to the maintainer before the affected writer, rather than being silently
introduced as a review correction.

#### Four implementation steps after acceptance

| Step | Coherent deliverable | Principal proof |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Accept/reconcile G9 carriers, implement immutable definition lifecycle/admitted form profile and independent append-only personal consent foundation | Domain/validator dirty-clean cases, target-qualified indexes, real app-role isolation/publication and consent sequencing/admission, same-transaction audit failure |
| 2 | Add MembershipProfile pins/value commands, exact contract readers, revision-aware disclosure/consent checks and diagnostic protection | Historical successors/retirement, required/null/remove behavior, withdrawal/write races, no raw JSONB path, actual nested canaries and positive sink/capture controls |
| 3 | Generate OpenAPI/SDK, activate exact native operations and scoped Studio/member/self-consent experience | Actual native HTTPS/provider/browser and non-JS paths where applicable, finite payload/Origin/CSRF/ETag/replay/session fences, enabled-locale/a11y/recovery behavior |
| 4 | Qualify combined packet, update delivered docs and prepare the P03-5 PR | Relevant complete local suites, two fresh review rounds, complete final-source CI A/B and original-archive reconciliation; truthful manual proof and open-boundary reporting |

The decision is accepted before Step 1's code. Each step is committed before its
first review; verified findings are fixed/committed and the second round uses
different reviewers. Security, correctness, privacy, UX/accessibility and bounded
performance are assigned to the relevant round, not multiplied into tiny steps.
No next step waits for another user prompt unless an actual decision/blocker needs
the maintainer. P03-5 finishes before its PR is opened; no merge is authorized.

#### Proposed HTTP and application census

All paths below have `/api/v1` as their prefix. Identity/tenancy scope comes only
from admitted context. The native dispatcher exposes distinct same-origin POST
operations bound to these exact API methods; it admits no caller-supplied URL.
Reads retain their actual API GET/HEAD treatment and explicit audit policy.

| API method and suffix | Exact request family | Admission |
|---|---|---|
| GET `/customization/custom-field-definitions` | `ListCustomFieldDefinitionsQuery` | Tenant custom-field admin; concept summaries, bounded cursor/status filter |
| GET `/customization/custom-field-definitions/{id}` | `GetCustomFieldDefinitionQuery` | Tenant custom-field admin; exact retained revision |
| GET `/customization/custom-field-definitions/{id}/revisions` | `ListCustomFieldDefinitionRevisionsQuery` | Tenant custom-field admin; exact target/concept, cursor 20 |
| POST `/customization/custom-field-definitions` | `RegisterCustomFieldDefinitionCommand` | Tenant custom-field admin, orgless; creates Draft |
| PUT `/customization/custom-field-definitions/{id}` | `ReviseCustomFieldDefinitionDraftCommand` | Same; Draft only, strong If-Match |
| POST `/customization/custom-field-definitions/{id}/publication` | `PublishCustomFieldDefinitionCommand` | Same; strong If-Match and exact expected incumbent/absence |
| POST `/customization/custom-field-definitions/{id}/retirement` | `RetireCustomFieldDefinitionCommand` | Same; Active only, strong If-Match |
| POST `/customization/custom-field-definitions/{id}/discard` | `DiscardCustomFieldDefinitionDraftCommand` | Same; Draft only, strong If-Match, no hard delete/key reuse |
| GET `/identity/memberships/{id}/custom-fields` | `GetMembershipCustomFieldsQuery` | Existing exact admin member-read predicate; MUST sensitive read |
| GET `/identity/me/custom-fields` | `GetOwnMembershipCustomFieldsQuery` | Exact current own Membership read; Off |
| PATCH `/identity/memberships/{id}/custom-fields` | `SetMembershipCustomFieldsCommand` | Existing exact admin profile-write predicate; strong Membership If-Match |
| PATCH `/identity/me/custom-fields` | `SetOwnMembershipCustomFieldsCommand` | Existing exact own profile-write predicate; no client-selected Membership; strong If-Match |
| GET `/tenancy/membership-field-consents/own` | `GetOwnMembershipFieldConsentQuery` | Own Membership only; exact definition pin, Off |
| GET `/tenancy/membership-field-consents/own/scopes` | `ListOwnFieldConsentScopesQuery` | Host-capped retained subject scopes under OwnConsentEntry, cursor 20, Off |
| GET `/tenancy/membership-field-consents/own/history` | `ListOwnMembershipFieldConsentsQuery` | Exact retained owned scope under OwnConsentEntry; latest tuple state, cursor 20, Off |
| POST `/tenancy/membership-field-consents/grants` | `GrantOwnMembershipFieldConsentCommand` | Closed own-consent policy; expected predecessor and explicit confirmation |
| POST `/tenancy/membership-field-consents/withdrawals` | `WithdrawOwnMembershipFieldConsentCommand` | OwnConsentEntry retained subject scope; expected predecessor and explicit confirmation, no Active Membership |

Every mutation is MUST-audited and idempotent with freshly authorized replay.
Consent POSTs use the same protected keyed replay family, including their exact
predecessor; an exact replay does not append and is a historical receipt, while
a different-key stale predecessor conflicts. New P03-5 bodies use the versioned
HMAC path selected in ADR-0095; all historical fingerprints remain unchanged.
Definition publication binds both the Draft version and expected incumbent; the
absent-incumbent case is explicit. Duplicate/unknown operation names, keys, pins,
targets and fields refuse before mutation. A value request carries bounded
explicit set/remove operations and a complete-required-field assertion checked
against the server's effective result; omitted stored slots are not removed.
Explicit removal-only requests bypass completeness and expose the remaining
missing-field state; an unanswered field cannot prevent clearing another value.
Definition schemas used by a form travel through Identity's authorized projection,
not an unaudited broad definition directory exposed to every learner.
Studio owns `/studio/custom-fields` and its exact-revision detail editor; the
existing `/studio/members/{membershipId}` detail receives the member form. The
existing `/portal/profile` receives own values, purpose notices and personal
consent controls without requiring Studio access. Schema payloads are JSON
objects, not recursively escaped JSON strings; projection/page serialization
retains the actual 256 KiB response and existing shared snapshot budget guards.
Own-consent history remains reachable from Portal even when no Active definition
or stored value points to that grant; withdrawal is not a hidden exact-ID API.
After lifecycle loss, `/account/consents` and the closed native entry POSTs
`/api/auth/entry/consents` and `/api/auth/entry/consents/withdraw` use an existing
credentialed entry handle and fixed consent-only shell, independent of public
site/CurrentSession admission. Ordinary grant still requires Active Membership.

#### Acceptance and reconciliation inventory

Step 1 lands the ADR acceptance and G9 answer first, then current canonical

### P03-5 proposal review round 1 and corrections (2026-11-10)

Two fresh independent reviewers inspect proposal commit `94f5a6d6` against the
current corpus/code: Sol high for contract/privacy/authorization and Terra high
for experience/transport/performance. This is static proposal review, not runtime
qualification. They verify two Major defects; both are corrected before approval:

- The 4 KiB submission limit and complete-required-set rule allowed definitions
  that no empty Profile could answer: one required 4,096-character string, or
  twenty required 256-character strings, already exceed the budget with pins.
  The proposal now requires a conservative per-field admission and aggregate
  publication proof including canonical serialization/escaping/encoded overhead.
  An impossible/unprovable required set refuses before replacing the incumbent.
  Actual byte checks remain; no staged-save or larger transport is introduced.
- Consent eligibility did not distinguish a new grant from withdrawal. A grant
  could commit, its later value save fail, and retirement leave no retained pin,
  preventing withdrawal. Existing exact consent tuple reads/withdrawals now
  require neither a retained value nor an Active definition. New grants for
  Deprecated revisions still require a retained pin. Reconsent's effect on
  retained-value disclosure is explicit; the original write evidence is immutable.

The plan adds behavioral boundary/rollback cases for both findings and a 32 KiB
stored collection limit. Proposed own-consent admission requires a current Active
Membership; post-membership-loss subject request authority stays with P03-10.
No schema, runtime writer or Accepted ADR body changes in this correction.

### P03-5 proposal review round 2 and corrections (2026-11-10)

Two different fresh reviewers inspect `ebb33739`: Terra high for security,
privacy and ownership; Sol high for experience, numeric fidelity and transport.
They verify the first-round corrections and identify three further Major gaps.
The proposal and exact census now address all three:

- An unchanged sensitive pin counts toward requiredness only while the latest
  consent for its exact tuple is Granted. Withdrawal makes it both withheld and
  incomplete. Mixed set/remove and explicit reconsent receive behavioral cases;
  removal-only remains independent of completeness.
- Exact-pin consent read/withdrawal eligibility was insufficient for discovery.
  The packet adds `ListOwnMembershipFieldConsentsQuery` and a bounded own-history
  route/Portal control, including successful grant plus failed save plus later
  retirement with no retained value. Current-Membership tuple pages resolve
  retained notices in an owning-contract batch, without a broad directory or
  N+1 query. A person can find and withdraw that grant after fresh navigation.
- Finite JSON numbers alone do not preserve browser fidelity: the current SDK
  and snapshot paths use JSON.parse/stringify and can round unsafe integers.
  The selected profile uses safe integers and explicit finite binary64 number
  semantics, rejects overflow/underflow/integer precision loss, and requires
  normalized schema/value round trips through actual server/native/form paths.
  Boundary, nested and direct API-to-Portal controls qualify this policy in code;
  no arbitrary-precision/exact-decimal field or larger body is selected.

Whole-value diagnostic exclusion also names validation/L1 error responses
separately from legitimate authorized value responses. Structural error indices
do not echo tenant-authored keys or labels. This is a static contract correction;
runtime safety, actual user journeys and performance remain implementation proof.
ADR-0095 stays Proposed and G9 stays Open pending the maintainer's explicit choice.

### P03-5 proposal correction verification and approval readiness (2026-11-10)

The two round-2 reviewers independently verify their respective corrections in
`a55cf09a`: latest-Granted requiredness, discoverable consent-only history and
numeric round-trip boundaries close the verified findings without a contradictory
replacement. Their verification is bounded and static, not a third broad review
or runtime qualification. Both round-1 findings are also covered by the revised
contract and the named dirty/clean implementation cases.

Document controls pass: 3,470 Markdown fragment links resolve, roadmap structure

The changed paths are exactly the ADR, decision index, glossary, phase Status and
this log. Development remains selected; tracked source is unchanged and the

The maintainer is asked to approve ADR-0095 and the four-step package, including
immutable Membership-only fields, bounded nested forms, requiredness independent
of admission, separate personal consent/withdrawal, explicit registry-v3 grant
adoption and the stated size/numeric/history costs. No schema, runtime writer,

the requested commit/two-fresh-review cycle and stops only for an actual new
decision or external blocker. Existing packet evidence follow-ups stay separate.

### P03-5 maintainer review disposition and revised contract (2026-11-10)

The maintainer supplies external reviews and directs the implementation owner
to verify findings, correct the documents, accept the result and proceed. This
is conditional approval of the corrected coupled contract, not acceptance of
every suggested mechanism or a runtime-proof claim. The owner compares the
findings with real schema, permission, replay, entry and scope implementations;
two focused read-only Sol/Terra investigations corroborate the new authority and
fingerprint seams. Verified corrections are:

- The finite form profile has a closed per-type keyword grammar, no formats or
  schema annotations, explicit container units and constructive nonemptiness
  witnesses validated by the actual existing evaluator. Both satisfiability and
  individual/combined serialization feasibility precede publication.
- Standard 05 owns the new lock consumers. Shared value and exclusive definition
  fencing provide final-read-through-COMMIT Active eligibility; the older content
  reader contract remains unchanged. Both winner orders need real PostgreSQL proof.
- Consent withdrawal/history no longer depends on Active Membership, live public
  content or an ordinary BFF session. A separate retained-subject entry has one
  confined Tenancy-only definer and one logical setter, giving twelve of each
  while preserving four physical writers, existing roles and three global-self
  descriptors. Its fixed shell/entry owner cannot disclose values or confer scope.
- Consent scope derives from authoritative Membership at grant and retained
  consent at withdrawal. Exact notice locale/hash, purpose grammar, typed root,
  RLS/filter/marker/grant/census and root-specific audit semantics are explicit.
- New body-bearing P03-5 replay uses a scoped versioned HMAC key ring; existing
  fingerprint bytes remain unchanged. Derived linkage, expired physical rows,
  key loss/rotation/restore, WAL/backups and P03-10 ownership are accounted for.
- Registry v3 is exactly v2 plus one pair; v2 must precede v3. Its single-key
  delta preserves earlier nonkernel removals. SQL/seed/fingerprint history and
  both discoverable transitions require forward-compatible implementation.
- Partial value mutation is PATCH with distinct own/admin requests. A bounded
  concept revision-history route avoids client-wide scans. Consent predecessor
  and same-key replay semantics, tenth-capability source/activation and Standard
  10 diagnostic ownership are included in the exact reconciliation inventory.
- Schema/input caps are independent aggregate ceilings, not reservations. The
  schema sublimit is 2 KiB; full input stays 4 KiB. Remaining capacity, encoded
  bytes, optional-value 32 KiB sharing and pure-removal remediation are visible.
- Retained definitions have 100 concepts/1,000 revisions/20 live Drafts, without
  pretending discard frees history. Consent history deliberately remains retained
  lifetime evidence; same-state no-append and a durable sixty-second grant
  cooldown bound toggling. Withdrawal has no grant cooldown; existing subject/
  visitor limits remain. Phase 11 owns operational retention, not automatic
  compaction of evidence; P03-10 owns separately authorized subject fulfillment.

Suggestions rejected or narrowed with evidence:

- None is already an explicit PersonalDataCategory and is permitted by G9.
  Excluding all None values from DSAR/erasure is not authorized: subject linkage
  and purpose still matter. Add a positive None control, not an export bypass.
- `IAuditSubject.Designate(successor)` is required when publication tracks two
  same-type roots; replacing that sentence with lifecycle prose would remove a
  real audit invariant. The corrected wording retains both lifecycle and call.
- Standards receive canonical updates derived from ADR-0095, not ADR amendment
  headings. ADR-0074 gets navigation only. ADR-0037/0044/0077 mechanics apply
  unchanged; new consumers/slugs go into their owning matrices/catalogues.
- An unconditional switch to per-tuple locking would not fence consent withdrawal
  against existing Tenant-fenced value writes. This packet retains the coupled
  shared/exclusive protocol and acknowledges serialization/storage costs.

No code or migration is included in this disposition. It supersedes proposal
claims in earlier records where explicitly different, without rewriting those
historical review verdicts. The corrected ADR and current package govern the
